purpose: Campaign slice 3 — status row truth owned by ds-command-kernel. Each case holds one `design_status_row` request, what the deleted TypeScript answered for it (`expected_ts`: `statusRowView`, `mergeLocalTransformerStatus`, `supersededPhase`, `latestAction`, `transformerGovernanceBadge`, `canRetryProcess`, the three row-name sets — recorded by running that code once before deleting it), and what the kernel answers (`expected`). A case where the two differ carries a `why`; the kernel is right in every one. `label_rename` is the vocabulary table that makes the two comparable — the kernel returns i18n KEYS where the browser returned English. Since 2026-09-22 there is one way to process a transformer: the kernel answers no `lane`, `phase_lanes`, `legacy_standard_output` or per-stamp `lane`, so those members of `expected_ts` are retired and not compared. The accepted baseline migration at a8f6386 is accounted separately in baseline_migration; historical expected_ts values are retained, and baseline_cases prove pinned zero and missing-evidence behavior.

cases.why: CORRECTION. The live edit-lock badge used to be painted beside the governance badge by StatusTable.svelte, so `transformerGovernanceBadge` and `governanceFilterValue` never saw it: the row read Locked in the name cell and `draft` in the governance filter and the Dashboard's governance mix at the same time. The lock is a host FACT fed in now (`local_edit_lock`), so one answer covers the badge, the filter and the mix. `locally_overridden` marks it, and it is reachable only from Open — an override never reports a lock the server already denies.

cases.why: CORRECTION, and the defect this row exists for. `canRetryProcess` returned true from `hasSavedLayers(tr)` BEFORE consulting ds-brain, so a client-side layer count overruled a published `retry_capabilities.process.can_retry === false` (api/design.ts's own comment: "Frontends should prefer this over inferring"). The published verdict is authoritative when present; the layer count may answer only for older documents that carry no verdict. The refusal is named: `reason: backend_refused`.

cases.why: One canonicalisation. `isVersionableTransformer` trimmed and lowercased but did not fold punctuation, so ' Combined-Transformer ' missed `UNVERSIONABLE_NAMES` and was reported versionable while `isSpecialRow` — which DID fold punctuation — called the same row special. `design::canonical_row_name` is the one rule all four predicates read.

specials.name: __all__
specials.why: `__all__` is the project-wide selection token, never a register row: `isSpecialRow` answered false for it only because the set that listed it (`UNVERSIONABLE_NAMES`) was a different set from the one that defined special. Under one vocabulary it is the aggregate it has always been. No caller asks `isSpecialRow('__all__')` — the register only classifies names it renders.

specials.name: combined_transformers
specials.why: The plural spelling the report lane already reserved (`is_reserved_report_identity`) while the register's three sets did not list it at all — so the same name was an aggregate to Rust and a transformer to the browser. It is one aggregate now.

A nameless row is a target of nothing. `isVersionableTransformer` said so first ('' is not versionable) while `canTargetForCombined` said the opposite because its set simply did not contain the empty string. The four predicates agree now.
Whitespace canonicalises to the empty name; see the empty-name divergence.
